analysis.summary: Crude oil prices fell sharply (7%) following U.S.-Iran diplomatic signals, removing geopolitical war premium and pressuring integrated energy majors' upstream and refining margins. Meanwhile, energy transition investments accelerate with LNG terminal development in Pakistan and hydrogen-blending trials, signaling a structural shift away from pure-play oil exposure. Near-term outlook is bearish for traditional oil & gas producers due to price weakness, but longer-term opportunities exist for diversified energy companies.

Further OPEC+ production cuts could offset price declines and support margins
Energy transition investments may cannibalize fossil fuel demand faster than priced in
Houthi attacks on Saudi refinery demonstrate ongoing supply chain vulnerabilities in key regions
